raw_response:
I am 59 years old, been working this same dirt since I was a boy. My father did wheat-maize, I do wheat-maize. Ten mu and a bit — not big, not small. The well is good, water comes when I need it.

Here is how I think about this year. Last year was alright. Wheat gave me maybe 450 kg per mu, maize close to 550. Not the best in the village but not the worst. Old Wang next to my plot, he got more on maize because he put extra urea — I saw him carry the bags. Maybe I do a little more this time too.

For wheat I plant in October like always. Before plowing I spread two bags of the compound stuff — the 15-15-15 the dealer in town sells — that is one bag for half my field, so about half a bag per mu, around 25 kg per mu. Then in spring when the wheat starts standing tall I broadcast urea, maybe 15 kg per mu, before an irrigation. The water carries it down. I water the wheat four times — once before winter so it does not freeze dry, then jointing, then when the head comes out, then when the grain is filling. If rain comes I skip one. Spray two times for aphids and the rust, the shop sells the mix.

For maize after wheat harvest in June, I plant the hybrid seed — same kind Old Wang uses, the bag has a red picture. I put compound in the row when planting, half a bag per mu again. Then when the maize is knee-high I side-dress urea, a good amount, maybe 20 kg per mu because maize eats more than wheat. Water once or twice if July is dry, our summer rain usually does most of it. Spray once for borer.

I use the rotary tiller man — he comes with the machine, costs less than plowing deep. Everyone uses him now.

I do not want to skimp on fertilizer. If I save 50 yuan and lose 100 kg of grain, that is stupid. Better put a little extra and sleep easy.
